ledger.contains: MOU (11 pp.) between DOJ Antitrust Division, USPS and USPS OIG creating the Whistleblower Rewards Program: authority (39 U.S.C. 404(a)(7) lets USPS pay informers one-half of penalties; 39 U.S.C. 2601), intake and evaluation procedure, eligibility threshold (criminal fine of at least $1 million or equivalent DPA/NPA recovery), reward presumption at least 15% and maximum 30% of the recovered criminal fine (also the cap for several whistleblowers together), worked example ($2 million fine, 20% = $400,000, $800,000 remitted to USPS), definitions (eligible whistleblower, voluntary, original information, 120-day internal-reporting window, 120-day exception for compliance staff), eligible criminal violations, ten award factors, general provisions (no funding obligation, 30-day termination notice), signatures dated 7 May 2025. Footnote 1 gives Sherman Act maximum penalties (10 years; $1 million individuals; $100 million corporations), which are about antitrust law, not the programme. The worked example is illustrative, not data. Already in the data: 4 rules (min, max, discretionary, threshold) and the signing event. Added: anonymous filing via attorney, 120-day internal-reporting window.

Antitrust Division web page on the Whistleblower Rewards Program (no publication date in the saved copy): what antitrust crimes are, partnership with USPIS and USPS OIG, eligibility ($1 million fines or recoveries), presumptive award 15-30%, discretion, how to report (yourself or through an attorney, by email), FAQ on confidentiality, CAARA 2019 anti-retaliation protection via OSHA, leniency programme, what to include in a report. No statistics. Added the four reward rules and a CAARA event. The page says a report may go through an attorney but does not say it may be anonymous, so no anonymous_filing row.

DOJ press release 09-831 (21 Aug 2009): Bradley Birkenfeld sentenced to 40 months; guilty plea 19 June 2008; his help to a US billionaire evade $7.2 million in taxes on $200 million of hidden assets (numbers about the crime, not the programme); UBS deferred prosecution agreement Feb 2009; 19 Aug 2009 settlement of the John Doe summons (4,450 more customers); officials' quotes; FBAR and Schedule B disclosure rules (accounts over $10,000, not programme). The release does not mention whistleblower status or any reward. Already in the data: plea and sentencing events. Added: UBS DPA (month) and John Doe settlement events.

DOJ press release (7 Jan 2021, page updated 5 Feb 2025): Boeing deferred prosecution agreement for conspiracy to defraud the FAA AEG over MCAS; over $2.5 billion ($243.6 million penalty, $1.77 billion to airline customers, $500 million crash-victim fund; 346 deaths, 189 and 157 on the two flights); facts of the deception, crash dates, grounding (13 Mar 2019), cooperation and remediation factors, no monitor. No whistleblower or reward content. Already in the data: the settlement case and the DPA event; nothing else in scope.

DOJ press release (13 Dec 2022): Danske Bank guilty plea to conspiracy to commit bank fraud; forfeiture of $2.059 billion ("$2 billion" in headline); DOJ credits about $850 million paid to the SEC and Danish authorities; $160 billion processed through US banks for non-resident customers (about the crime); by Feb 2014 the bank knew of suspicious transactions from audits, regulators and "an internal whistleblower"; resolution factors; SEC settlement of about $413 million incl. $178.6 million civil penalty. Already in the data: the DOJ case and the plea event. Added: the SEC settlement as its own case row.

Criminal Division memorandum (Galeotti, 12 May 2025, 8 pp.) on white-collar enforcement priorities: ten high-impact areas, amendments to the Corporate Whistleblower Awards Pilot subject areas (cartels/TCOs, immigration, material support of terrorism, sanctions, trade/tariff/customs fraud, procurement fraud), CEP revisions, shorter resolution terms (no longer than three years except rare cases), monitor policy. No programme numbers. Already in the data: the CWA expansion event; nothing else in scope.

DOJ fact sheet (3 pp., Aug 2024) launching the Corporate Whistleblower Awards Pilot: start date 1 Aug 2024, four initial subject areas, forfeiture over $1 million, awards up to 30% of first $100 million and 5% of $100-500 million net proceeds, presumption of 30% on the first $10 million, confidentiality, exclusion of meaningful participants, link to VSD programmes, 120-day internal-reporting window (and 120 days for companies under the CEP), plans to evaluate and seek legislation. No statistics. Already in the data: the launch event. Added six rules.

DOJ fact sheet (3 pp., Aug 2026): programme description, May 2025 expansion to four more priority areas, over 1,800 tips since launch (two years), new intake portal, eight subject areas, same award rules as 2024 (forfeiture over $1 million; 30% of first $100 million, 5% of $100-500 million; 30% presumption on first $10 million; 120-day internal-reporting window), confidentiality, exclusion of participants. Already in the data: the tips observation and two events. Added six rules. "A substantial number of promising tips" and "have led to criminal investigations" give no numbers.

Pilot Program guidance (1 Aug 2024, 14 pp.): legal basis (28 U.S.C. 524(c)); three-year pilot run by MLARS from 1 Aug 2024; eligibility and exclusions (entities, those eligible under other programmes, DOJ staff and family, foreign officials, meaningful participants, false statements); original information (incl. 120-day internal-report window and 120-day exception for compliance staff); four subject areas; voluntary, truthful, cooperation requirements; forfeiture over $1,000,000; award scale (up to 30% of first $100 million, up to 5% of $100-500 million, none above $500 million, 30% presumption on first $10 million); payment priority (victims first); factors that raise or lower awards; confidentiality; anonymous submission through an attorney; retaliation; permanent bar after three frivolous submissions; congressional notice of awards over $500,000 (28 U.S.C. 524(c)(2)); submission procedure (attorney must provide signed form within 7 days on request); 90-day claim window; award determinations not appealable. Already in the data: six rules. Added: 30% presumption threshold, 120-day internal-reporting window. Not recorded as rules (no fitting rule type): no award on net proceeds above $500 million (already in the notes of the 5% row), the $500,000 congressional-notification trigger, the three-submission bar, the 7-day attorney deadline. No statistics.

Pilot Program guidance as revised 30 July 2026 (15 pp.): same structure and award scale as the 2024 guidance, with these changes: section now named MLNFS; eligibility for another programme no longer bars an award, only duplicate awards (footnote 3, new factor III.3.b.v on other programmes); eight subject areas (adds federal health care offenses generally, federal contracting fraud, trade/tariff/customs fraud, immigration, sanctions/terrorism/cartels); submissions through the online intake portal. Already in the data: two events (launch, revision). Added eight rules restating the award terms (threshold, 30%/5% scale, 30% presumption on first $10 million, discretion, anonymous via attorney, 120-day internal window, 90-day claim window). Not recorded as rules (no fitting type): no award above $500 million net proceeds (in notes), $500,000 congressional-notification trigger (p. 14), three-submission bar, 7-day attorney deadline. No statistics.

Criminal Division web page (updated 31 July 2026): programme description, new online intake portal, eight subject areas, award as a percentage of forfeited assets in DOJ's sole discretion, confidentiality, companies that self-report within 120 days of an internal report may get a CEP declination (a company rule, not a whistleblower rule), links to guidance and fact sheet, award claim forms "available soon" (no award claims process open yet). No numbers on the programme. Added: discretionary rule.

DOJ ENRD Environmental Crimes Section Monthly Bulletin, May 2016 (20 pp.): case table; decisions (Aquarosa APPS whistleblower award of $550,000, contingency fee rejected, counsel fees beyond $10,000 referred to a magistrate judge); trials, indictments, guilty pleas and sentencings in environmental and wildlife cases (incl. APPS vessel cases Oceanic Illsabe, Bingham Fox and DSD/Stavanger Blossom with a $2 million fine and $500,000 community service payment, none mentioning a whistleblower or award); contacts; announcements. Only the Aquarosa item is in scope. Already in the data: the Aquarosa award case. Added: APPS half-of-fine rule as stated in the bulletin. The $10,000 counsel fee is not an award and is not recorded.

DOJ Civil Division fact sheet on FY2025 FCA settlements and judgments (7 pp., 16 Jan 2026): representative matters by area (managed care, prescription drugs, unnecessary services, military procurement, cybersecurity, pandemic fraud, tariff and customs) with about 40 named settlements, judgments and complaints and their amounts; cybersecurity: over $52 million in nine settlements in FY2025; pandemic: more than 200 settlements/judgments over $230 million in FY2025, over $820 million to date; Ceratizit $54.4 million customs settlement (after FY end). The FY2025 headline totals are not in this fact sheet. Already in the data: the Penelow v. Janssen event. Added: 3 recoveries observations and 3 relator cases (Penelow, Behnke, intervened Aetna/Elevance/Humana suit).

DOJ press release 98-503 (23 Oct 1998): more than $2 billion recovered in qui tam cases since 1986 ($1 billion by 1995); relator share rules (15-25% if US litigates, up to 30% alone); qui tam suits 33 in FY1987, 534 in FY1997, more than 2,400 in total; $2.249 billion total recoveries ($2.189 billion intervened, $60 million relator-litigated); about $300 million to whistleblowers; six named qui tam recoveries (HCSC, SmithKline, Roche, Damon, Mobil, Hercules). Already in the data: 8 observations. Added: 3 rules and 6 cases. The headline "more than $2 billion" is the rounded form of the $2.249 billion already recorded, so not repeated; "half of the recoveries have come in the last three years" is words, not a number.
